# Didache Chapter 10 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 10

---

## Chapter 10

**1** After you have been satisfied, give thanks in this way:

**2** We give you thanks, holy Father, for your holy name which you have caused to dwell in our hearts, and for the knowledge and faith and immortality which you made known to us through Jesus your servant. To you be glory forever.

**3** You, Lord Almighty, created all things for the sake of your name; you gave food and drink to human beings to enjoy, so that they might give you thanks. And to us you have graciously granted spiritual food and spiritual drink and eternal life, through Jesus your servant.

**4** Above all, we thank you because you are mighty. To you be glory forever.

**5** Remember, Lord, your Church — to rescue it from all evil and to make it perfect in your love, and gather it together from the four winds, now sanctified, into your kingdom which you have prepared for it. For yours is the power and the glory forever.

**6** Let grace come, and let this world pass away.
Hosanna to the God of David.
If any are holy, let them come; if any are not, let them repent.
Maranatha! [Our Lord, come!]
Amen.

**7** Allow the prophets to give thanks as they will.

---

### Council Notes

**On v.2 — κατεσκήνωσας ("caused to dwell"):** All agents preserve this tabernacle/shekinah language. God's name "dwelling" (σκηνόω) in the community's hearts is precisely the same verb used in John 1:14 ("the Word tabernacled among us"). This theological connection should be noted.

**On v.3 — "spiritual food and drink":** EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA all recognize this as the Didache's interpretation of the eucharistic elements. SOPHIA retains the phrase without further interpretation — it is the text's own word for what is being shared.

**On v.5 — "perfect" vs. "whole":** τελειώσῃ = to bring to completion/perfection. EMET uses "perfect in your love"; LOGOS "make it perfect"; PNEUMA "bring to wholeness." SOPHIA adopts "make it perfect in your love" — this use of τέλειος in a prayer context (requesting divine perfection) is distinct from its ethical use in chs. 1 and 6.

**On v.6 — Maranatha! [Our Lord, come!]:** All agents unanimously preserve the Aramaic untranslated with the gloss, per the project brief. This is our ruling. The phrase appears also in 1 Cor 16:22 and (in Greek translation) in Rev 22:20. Preserving the Aramaic honors the antiquity of the prayer.

**On v.6 — "Hosanna to the God of David":** SOPHIA notes that this acclamation is unique — Hosanna is normally addressed to the Son of David (Matt 21:9), not to God himself. The Didache's "God of David" is a distinctive formulation, grounding the messianic hope in God the Father's covenant with David.

**On v.7 — prophets' freedom:** All agents agree. This verse is a significant datum for understanding early charismatic ministry: written liturgical prayers are the baseline, but inspired prophets are free to pray beyond them.
